accepted.s: The Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 was substantially influenced by the recommendations of which committee constituted in 1962?
o: Gorwala Committee
Santhanam Committee
Hota Committee
Sarkaria Committee
accepted.x: The Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption was constituted in 1962 and its recommendations contributed to stronger anti-bribery laws, eventually consolidated in the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
accepted.tq: Identify the committee associated with the legislative development.
accepted.sec: Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 and 2018 amendment - changes

accepted.s:
Under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, the expression ‘public servant’ includes which of the following?
1. An employee of a local authority
2. A Judge
3. A person whose office requires performance of a public duty
4. Only a permanent employee of the Union Government
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: The definition in Section 2(c) covers government and local-authority employees, Judges and persons performing a public duty. It is not restricted to permanent Union Government employees.
accepted.tq: Reject the restrictive word ‘only’ and identify the statutory scope of a definition.
accepted.sec: Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 and 2018 amendment - changes

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT specifically identified as an offence under the Prevention of Corruption Act in the material under consideration?
o: Defamation
Bribery
Undue advantage
Criminal misconduct
accepted.x: Bribery, undue advantage and criminal misconduct are identified offences under the Act. Defamation is not included in this list.
accepted.tq: Find the term outside the statutory offence cluster.
accepted.sec: Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 and 2018 amendment - changes

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 2018 amendment to the Prevention of Corruption Act:
1. Giving a bribe was made a direct offence.
2. A coerced bribe-giver may receive protection if the bribe is reported within seven days.
3. Commercial organisations may be liable for bribes offered on their behalf.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The 2018 amendment made bribe-giving a direct offence, protected a coerced giver reporting within seven days, and imposed liability on commercial organisations for bribes offered on their behalf.
accepted.tq: Test a legislative amendment through a complete set of related changes.
accepted.sec: Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 and 2018 amendment - changes

accepted.s: The offence concerning bribe-giving under the amended Prevention of Corruption Act may attract imprisonment of up to:
o: Ten years
Four years
Two years
Seven years
accepted.x: The amended framework treats bribe-giving as a direct offence punishable with imprisonment of up to seven years.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact punishment figure from a reform provision.
accepted.sec: Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 and 2018 amendment - changes

accepted.s: The expression ‘undue advantage’ became central to the framing of offences under which measure?
o: The original Constitution of India
The 2018 amendment to the Prevention of Corruption Act
The CVC Act, 2003
The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013
accepted.x: The 2018 amendment to the Prevention of Corruption Act framed the relevant bribery offence around the concept of ‘undue advantage’.
accepted.tq: Match the precise statutory expression with the correct amendment.
accepted.sec: Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 and 2018 amendment - changes

accepted.s: Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act relates to:
o: Appointment of the Central Vigilance Commissioner
Prior government approval before inquiry or investigation into official decisions of a public servant
Automatic transfer of corruption cases to the Supreme Court
Protection of every private citizen from prosecution
accepted.x: Section 17A requires prior government approval before an inquiry or investigation into a public servant concerning decisions taken in the discharge of official functions.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority or procedural safeguard applies to the described official decision.
accepted.sec: Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 and 2018 amendment - changes

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the differing views in the split verdict concerning Section 17A?
o: Justice Nagarathna struck it down as violating Article 14, while Justice Viswanathan upheld it subject to a binding Lokpal or Lokayukta opinion.
Justice Nagarathna upheld it, while Justice Viswanathan struck it down as violating Article 19.
Both judges upheld it without attaching any condition to approval.
Both judges struck it down solely because it concerned retired public servants.
accepted.x: Justice Nagarathna held Section 17A unconstitutional as violating Article 14. Justice Viswanathan upheld it on the condition that approval rests on a binding Lokpal or Lokayukta opinion; the matter is pending before a larger Bench.
accepted.tq: Separate the contrasting judicial views instead of treating a split verdict as a unanimous ruling.
accepted.sec: Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 and 2018 amendment - changes

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Vineet Narain — 1997
2. Subramanian Swamy — 2014
3. Centre for PIL v. Union of India — 2026
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Vineet Narain was decided in 1997, Subramanian Swamy in 2014, and Centre for PIL v. Union of India produced the noted split verdict in 2026.
accepted.tq: Match landmark cases with their years and use the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 and 2018 amendment - changes

accepted.s: A public servant is prosecuted for an offence of bribery under the amended Prevention of Corruption Act. Which of the following correctly states the punishment and trial framework mentioned?
o: Imprisonment of three to seven years and trial within two years, extendable up to a maximum of four years
Imprisonment of one to three years and trial within seven years without extension
Fine alone, with no prescribed time limit for trial
Imprisonment of seven to ten years and trial only after retirement
accepted.x: A bribed public servant may receive three to seven years’ imprisonment and a fine. Trials are intended to conclude within two years, with extension possible up to a maximum of four years.
accepted.tq: Combine punishment and procedural time limits without confusing the two periods.
accepted.sec: Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 and 2018 amendment - changes

accepted.s: The 2018 amendment to the Prevention of Corruption Act was intended, among other things, to align Indian law with:
o: The UN Convention against Corruption
The UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
The Geneva Convention on Refugees
The Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court
accepted.x: The 2018 amendment was intended to align the Prevention of Corruption Act with the United Nations Convention against Corruption, which India ratified in 2011.
accepted.tq: Identify the international instrument linked to a domestic legislative reform.
accepted.sec: Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 and 2018 amendment - changes

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the composition of the Lokpal?
o: A Chairperson and up to eight members, with 50% judicial members and at least 50% representation from SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women
Only a serving Chief Justice of India and four Governors
A Chairperson and exactly eight non-judicial members, all appointed by Parliament
A Chairperson and two Vigilance Commissioners without any representational requirement
accepted.x: The Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and up to eight members. Half the members are judicial, and at least half must be from SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women.
accepted.tq: Use composition, judicial share and representational requirements together to identify the correct body.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - composition, jurisdiction, selection, first Lokpal

accepted.s:
The selection committee for appointment of the Lokpal includes which of the following?
1. Prime Minister
2. Speaker of the Lok Sabha
3. Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
4. Chief Justice of India or the Chief Justice’s nominee
5. An eminent jurist
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1, 3, 4 and 5 only
2, 3, 4 and 5 only
accepted.x: The selection committee comprises the Prime Minister, Lok Sabha Speaker, Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition, Chief Justice of India or nominee, and an eminent jurist.
accepted.tq: Check the complete membership of a constitutional or statutory selection committee.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - composition, jurisdiction, selection, first Lokpal

accepted.s: The members of the Lokpal selection committee are appointed by the:
o: President of India
Chief Justice of India
Prime Minister of India
Speaker of the Lok Sabha
accepted.x: The members of the Lokpal selection committee are appointed by the President of India.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who appoints’ test to distinguish selection from appointment authority.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - composition, jurisdiction, selection, first Lokpal

accepted.s: Complaints under the Lokpal framework are required to be filed within how many years of the alleged offence?
o: Three years
Seven years
Five years
Ten years
accepted.x: A complaint under the Lokpal framework must be filed within seven years of the offence.
accepted.tq: Recall the limitation period using the exact numerical figure.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - composition, jurisdiction, selection, first Lokpal

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: First Lokpal — Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose
First Lokpal began work — 27 March 2019
Lokpal inquiry and prosecution wings — fully staffed from the commencement of the Act
Group C and D complaints — Central Vigilance Commission
accepted.x: The Lokpal’s inquiry wing under Section 11 and its prosecution wing were reported as still not fully staffed. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the overstated institutional claim containing the false completion detail.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - composition, jurisdiction, selection, first Lokpal

accepted.s: In the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta framework, the Lokayukta primarily deals with:
o: International relations, while the Upa-Lokayukta deals with public order
Only judicial officers, while the Upa-Lokayukta deals with private citizens
Higher functionaries, while the Upa-Lokayukta deals with the rest
Only Group C and D employees, while the Upa-Lokayukta deals with Ministers
accepted.x: The Lokayukta has jurisdiction over higher functionaries, whereas the Upa-Lokayukta deals with the remaining categories covered by the state law.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two closely related offices by their functional jurisdiction.
accepted.sec: AP Lokayukta - Act, appointment, jurisdiction

accepted.s: The Central Vigilance Commission was originally established in 1964 by:
o: An executive resolution based on the advice of the Santhanam Committee
A constitutional amendment based on the Sarkaria Commission
A Supreme Court judgment based on the Administrative Reforms Commission
A Presidential ordinance based on the Mandal Commission
accepted.x: The CVC was set up in 1964 through an executive resolution on the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee. It later became a statutory body under the CVC Act, 2003.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original executive basis from the later statutory status.
accepted.sec: Central Vigilance Commission - basis, composition, CBI link

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the composition and tenure of the Central Vigilance Commission?
o: One Central Vigilance Commissioner and exactly four Vigilance Commissioners; five years without an age limit
One Central Vigilance Commissioner and up to two Vigilance Commissioners; four years or until attaining 65 years, whichever is earlier
A Chairperson and up to eight members; six years or until 70 years
The CVC consists only of the Home Minister and the Cabinet Secretary
accepted.x: The Commission consists of the Central Vigilance Commissioner and up to two Vigilance Commissioners. Their tenure is four years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
accepted.tq: Combine institutional composition with tenure and age limits.
accepted.sec: Central Vigilance Commission - basis, composition, CBI link

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Central Vigilance Commission is correct?
o: It directly conducts every criminal trial arising from corruption complaints.
It supervises the Election Commission in electoral matters and appoints all Lokayuktas.
It supervises the CBI in corruption cases and is the competent authority under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act.
It is a constitutional body with exclusive jurisdiction over State Government employees.
accepted.x: The CVC supervises the CBI in corruption cases and functions as the competent authority under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act. It is a statutory, not constitutional, body.
accepted.tq: Identify the body by linking its supervisory and statutory functions.
accepted.sec: Central Vigilance Commission - basis, composition, CBI link

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Santhanam Committee — Committee on Prevention of Corruption
2. CBI — 1963
3. CVC — 1964
4. Prevention of Corruption Act — 1988
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: The Santhanam Committee was the Committee on Prevention of Corruption; the CBI emerged in 1963, the CVC in 1964, and the Prevention of Corruption Act was enacted in 1988.
accepted.tq: Track the institutional sequence from committee recommendation to statutory law.
accepted.sec: Santhanam Committee - recommendations and outcomes

accepted.s: The Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption functioned during:
accepted.x: The K. Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption was constituted in 1962 and its report was submitted in 1964.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the committee’s period from the years of later institutional outcomes.
accepted.sec: Santhanam Committee - recommendations and outcomes

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes a social audit under MGNREGA?
o: A confidential audit conducted only by contractors
An audit conducted by the Gram Sabha
An audit conducted exclusively by the Central Vigilance Commission
A judicial audit conducted by the Supreme Court
accepted.x: Under MGNREGA, the Gram Sabha undertakes social audits, enabling community-level scrutiny of works and expenditure.
accepted.tq: Identify the citizen institution responsible for the oversight activity.
accepted.sec: Citizens' oversight - social audit, report cards, public hearings

accepted.s: Citizen Report Cards were pioneered in Bengaluru in the 1990s by the:
o: Central Vigilance Commission associated with K. Santhanam
Public Affairs Centre associated with Samuel Paul
Planning Commission associated with B. R. Ambedkar
Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan associated with Aruna Roy
accepted.x: Citizen Report Cards were developed by the Public Affairs Centre in Bengaluru in the 1990s under the leadership of Samuel Paul.
accepted.tq: Recall the institution, person, place and decade as a single civil-society initiative.
accepted.sec: Citizens' oversight - social audit, report cards, public hearings

accepted.s: Jan Sunwai, as a method of citizen oversight, is most closely associated with:
o: Lokpal inquiries in Maharashtra during the 2000s
CVC hearings in Delhi during the 1980s
MKSS public hearings in Rajasthan during the 1990s
SSAAT audits in Andhra Pradesh during the 1970s
accepted.x: Jan Sunwai refers to public hearings associated with the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan in Rajasthan during the 1990s.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the similarly public-facing mechanisms by organisation, place and decade.
accepted.sec: Citizens' oversight - social audit, report cards, public hearings
